meta.title: AI Is Running Out of Human Data. Here’s the Trade.
meta.speakers: Dave Moss, Chris Camillo, Jordan Giesige
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · human data as the scarce input · Reddit as the pure play · the Reddit-deal arbitrage · Amazon vs agentic shopping · who wins when agents sprawl · market uncertainty and AI in schools

snapshot: Show opens with the data-scarcity thesis: labs train on the same internet, now full of AI slop — *a photocopy of a photocopy* — so fresh human argument is the one input money can't print.

Opening stats: Claude now does **26%** of Anthropic's own research (under 1% in February), with 30,000 AI agents running experiments; a federal judge ruled 10 days ago that one lab can't scrape for free.
Chris's core trade is **Reddit (RDDT)**: he bought more during the show, calls it a moderate (not top-five) position, and expects licensing rates to rise sharply as deals renew.
Reddit fell on news that Meta announced a rival forum product; every host dismissed it — Threads already failed, and Meta's relationship-based graph doesn't fit interest-based forums.
Chris keeps a scenario trade ready: if Reddit gets a bid or a big licensing deal, a 5-10 minute window may open in Yelp and Shutterstock — a trade only, not an endorsement.
On Amazon (AMZN), agent compute is a huge AWS positive while agentic shopping could erode the ad layer; Chris is a large holder and leans bullish into earnings.
Chris closes with a caution: the most uncertain market of his decades (COVID aside) — keep leverage under control for days to weeks.
A long, heated detour on AI in schools (Chris pro-AI tools, Jordan pro pencil-and-paper) ends unresolved; both admit the evidence is thin.

themes.status: THESIS — HUMAN DATA IS THE SCARCE INPUT
themes.title: Model-on-model training makes fresh human argument the scarce asset
themes.lead: Chris's bet: labs will pay whatever it takes for permissioned human signal, and Reddit holds the broadest pile of it.
bullets: Opening framing: Claude does **26%** of Anthropic's research, up from under 1% in February, with 30,000 agents running experiments; a federal judge ruled 10 days ago that a lab can't scrape for free.
Hosts concede nobody can say with conviction how model collapse plays out — papers and opinions conflict — but locking up fresh, permissioned human data is a *no-brainer* for the labs.

Data owners: Google (GOOGL) has the advantage via YouTube video and email (hosts unsure email rights allow training); xAI has X data, which Jordan sees as narrow (tech, politics, finance) next to Reddit's breadth.
Reddit's CEO (heard on a podcast) pitches the data as highly human — arguments, differing opinions, use cases — and Reddit gives its data free to researchers but charges commercial users.

Alternatives fall short: buying old books teaches language but not current information; timely signal still comes from X, Reddit or TikTok. Chris expects dozens of big tech buyers and rising renewal prices.
Reddit stats: user growth slowed to about 7%, yet it says **5%** of all content ever written there came in the last quarter — Chris can't tell how much of that is AI-written.

Meta's announced Reddit rival hit the stock intraday (a 2.5% flash drop, half recovered); hosts say Threads already failed and Meta's personal-relationship graph doesn't suit interest-based forums. Yahoo Answers and Google's forum also failed; only Reddit and Stack Overflow stuck.

quote.text: I'm just bewildered that this company is not getting more eyeballs on it right now from the investor community.

themes.title: A prepared-mind trade: Reddit takeover or licensing news could pull Yelp and Shutterstock
themes.lead: Chris thinks Reddit eventually gets acquired or signs licensing deals at far higher rates, opening a brief arbitrage window in look-alike data names.
bullets: Scenario: Reddit is acquired, or announces one or more major licensing deals well above today's rates; Chris runs it even at an illustrative **20%** chance.
The window would be a few minutes in names valued similarly: Yelp (YELP) for real-person reviews and Shutterstock (SSTK) for photography; Stack Overflow is another data comp.
Dave dislikes Yelp and its data and prefers Google reviews; Chris agrees and wants Yelp only for a 5-10 minute trade.
Hosts note that a takeover of any one of these would lift the others on the news alone.
themes.watch: Chris frames this as scenario planning, not a position. He is long Reddit, the underlying that would trigger it.

names.name: Yelp (YELP)
names.blurb: Trade-only: a 5-10 minute move if Reddit gets a bid or big licensing deal; hosts dislike the company and its data.

names.name: Shutterstock (SSTK)
names.blurb: Photography data comp that should react in a smaller but similar way to a Reddit deal.

themes.title: Amazon: agents are a huge AWS tailwind and a possible hit to the ad layer
themes.lead: Chris sees agent compute as the biggest infrastructure positive since AI began, with agentic shopping the one risk to Amazon's advertising.
bullets: Agents consume huge compute through simultaneous token runs; compute prices still rise week over week, feeding AWS, Bedrock, Graviton and Trainium.
Agentic AI could demolish the advertising layer as we know it, but Chris expects infrastructure spend to make up for it **two or three times** over, and nothing to happen quickly.
Amazon is building its own agent: project Moonraker, the internal code name for a full agentic Alexa+ that executes multi-step tasks from a single request — backed by more shopper data than anyone.
Open questions: an agent-to-agent advertising model, and paid or preferential product placement. Chris expects management to tackle agentic shopping on the next earnings call.
Amazon designs its own chips, so it is not beholden to Nvidia purchases. Diesel prices and shipping probably cost Amazon this quarter.
An Anthropic IPO near $2T would help Amazon; Chris says most X commentary on the filing is wrong — a half-trillion spend is over 10 years and the losses are an accounting shift.
themes.watch: Chris is a large Amazon holder and bought more in the days before.

names.name: Amazon (AMZN)
names.blurb: Large holding; loves it more every day; bullish into the next earnings call.

themes.status: OPEN QUESTION — WHO CAPTURES AGENT VALUE
themes.title: Agent sprawl: four assistants, no sync, and unclear winners in agentic shopping
themes.lead: Hosts use several agents at once, find the experience fragmented, and can't say which software layer survives agentic shopping.
bullets: Dave runs four agents reading his email, each flagging different things, and wants someone to make them share what they know about him — or one to win.
Dave would prefer Apple win so the assistant runs on-device with private cloud compute; Siri on iOS 27 can act on what's on screen, such as adding to the calendar.

Chris let Muse read Instagram DMs; Instagram locked him out for a week after Muse scraped them every 15 minutes. Muse also can't read WhatsApp: its virtual computer lacks a persistent browser session.
Hosts want a sentinel layer that approves every action an agent takes on your behalf.
Shopify (SHOP) looks like an obvious beneficiary of agentic shopping, but each agent might clone its own storefront — Chris says value capture is mind-boggling to call.
themes.watch: Dave admits he is wary of granting agents email access while using four of them; Chris's Muse account was restricted by Meta's own Instagram.

names.name: Shopify (SHOP)
names.blurb: Obvious agentic-shopping beneficiary on paper, but agents might build their own storefronts.

names.name: Apple (AAPL)
names.blurb: Dave would prefer Apple win the agent battle with on-device processing.

themes.title: Chris has never felt a market this uncertain, and says to keep leverage low
themes.lead: The AI trade is whipsawing on unknowns — model pace, safety delays, debt — and Chris advises no overconfidence for days to weeks.
bullets: Chris, trading for decades, has felt this uncertain only briefly during COVID; the next few weeks bring Gemini, new models, a lab delaying a model as dangerous, and labs asking government to step in.
Bloom Energy (BE) swings about 12% a day and 9-13% in the latest days; hosts like it because it sits upstream — the world needs electricity whoever wins.
The real bubble, a host argues, is debt, not AI: US fiscal debt plus heavy borrowing to fund AI raises rate worries.
Chris fears model speed more than danger — markets and companies need time to adjust — and sees no competent regulator, while labs want rules so they can say they followed them.
Chris trims leverage and tells viewers: if you are overconfident or levered right now, that is too much.
Dave points to an energy episode with Jordan next week, since energy is the one theme that doesn't feel confusing.

quote.text: If you're investing with leverage right now, that is too much. Be careful.

names.name: Bloom Energy (BE)
names.blurb: Swings 9-13% a day; upstream power exposure is seen as the least confusing AI-adjacent trade; a host wishes they'd bought the dip.

themes.title: Heated debate: AI tools in school versus pencil and paper
themes.lead: Chris wants teenagers taught to wield AI; Jordan wants screens limited, and neither can produce hard evidence.
bullets: Chris sat through seven classes at his kids' high school open house and heard AI mentioned zero times — curriculum he calls 1970s-style.
Jordan argues any screen time hurts learning, handwriting beats keyboards for language, and AI belongs in one separate class; some districts are dropping laptops-for-all.
Chris cites Alpha School in Austin, where kids reportedly learn **5x** faster with AI tutoring and operate like 30-year-olds; Jordan wants the peer-reviewed study.
Chris says test scores and IQ are the wrong measure — impact on the world is — and calls peer-reviewed studies mostly biased; Jordan retorts that this is anti-science.
Both admit the evidence is weak (Chris: intuition; Jordan: hasn't studied it as much); Chris's fallback is that content creators and sports may matter most in 30 years.

quote.text: I want them in school actually learning how to learn.

themes.watch: Chris says he barely got through school and calls his college education a waste; Jordan cites unnamed books and studies.

takeaways.title: Size Reddit as a multi-year bet on human data, not a swing trade — sentiment swings on rival-product headlines (Meta) have so far reversed.
Pre-plan the Reddit-deal scenario: note Yelp and Shutterstock as 5-10 minute reaction names, not holdings.
Cut leverage while AI news flow is erratic; the host's own guidance is days-to-weeks caution.
Separate Amazon's AWS compute tailwind from its ad-layer exposure when judging agentic shopping.
Gate every agent action behind approval before granting access to email or DMs.
Ask your school how AI fits the curriculum; both sides here agree the answer is unclear.
